question.text: A PMS portfolio drifts from 60% equity target to 55% equity after a correction. Under a rebalancing rule that triggers only when drift exceeds 5 percentage points (i.e., strictly more than 5%), the PM should:

answer.text: Ignore — drift is within the +/-5 percentage-point band
Rebalance immediately because it hit the 5% threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: The drift is 60% - 55% = 5 percentage points, exactly at the threshold. Under a "more-than-5%" trigger, equality does not breach the band, so no rebalancing action is required. NISM-Series-XXI-A pp. 135-136 describe threshold-based rebalancing rules that are activated only once the allocation drifts beyond the stated band. The Trap: Option B is the defensible reading under a "5% or more" trigger, which is why the audit flagged the original stem as ambiguous. Options C and D are absurd actions that ignore any disciplined rebalancing rule. Note: The original wording "Under a 5% threshold-based rebalancing rule" did not specify whether 5 percentage points triggers rebalancing or only sub-5% drift is ignored. The stem now explicitly states the trigger is "strictly more than 5%", which makes option A uniquely correct. (Source: NISM-Series-XXI-A PMS workbook, pp. 135-136.)
